title: Inversion (1)
summary: Инверсия после отрицательных и ограничительных наречий: **never, rarely, seldom, little, hardly ... when, no sooner ... than, not only, not until, only after, under no circumstances**.
ru:
## Что такое инверсия после наречий
Обычный порядок слов — подлежащее, потом сказуемое: *I have never seen it.* Если в начало предложения вынести **отрицательное или ограничительное наречие** (never, rarely, hardly, not only...), мы получаем **инверсию**: вспомогательный глагол выходит вперёд, подлежащее — за ним, как в вопросе, но предложение остаётся утвердительным.
> I have **never** seen such a beautiful sunset. → **Never have I** seen such a beautiful sunset. — Никогда я не видел такого красивого заката.
> She **rarely** complains. → **Rarely does she** complain. — Она редко жалуется.
Инверсия придаёт речи выразительность и официальность; её много в письменной речи, ораторских выступлениях и в формальных текстах, а в обыденной беседе она звучит книжно.

## Как строится инверсия
1. Наречие в начале предложения.
2. Вспомогательный (или модальный) глагол: *have, had, was, is, can, should, must*...
3. Подлежащее.
4. Основной глагол.
Если вспомогательного глагола в обычном предложении нет (Present Simple, Past Simple), добавляем **do / does / did** и основной глагол становится инфинитивом: *She never lies.* → *Never does she lie.* *They rarely came.* → *Rarely did they come.* Для глагола **be** ничего добавлять не нужно: *Rarely is he late.*

## Какие наречия вызывают инверсию
- **Отрицательные и частотные**: **never, rarely, seldom, hardly ever, nowhere, at no time, in no way, on no account, under no circumstances**.
> **Under no circumstances should** you open this door. — Ни при каких обстоятельствах не открывайте эту дверь.
> **Nowhere is** the problem more serious than in the south. — Нигде проблема не стоит так остро, как на юге.
- **little** (в значении «совсем не»): ***Little did** he know that the company was about to collapse.*
- **hardly / scarcely ... when** и **no sooner ... than** (оба — «едва... как»): ***Hardly had** she left **when** he called.* — ***No sooner had** she left **than** he called.* После no sooner — **than**, после hardly / scarcely — **when**; в первой части обычно Past Perfect.
- **not only ... but (also)**: ***Not only did** he apologise, **but** he also sent flowers.* Инверсия — только в первой части.
- **not until / only after / only when / only then / only by**: ***Not until** the 1960s **did** the idea become popular.* — ***Only then did** I realise my mistake.* — ***Only by working** hard **can** you succeed.* Инверсия идёт в **главной** части, а не в придаточной с until/after/when: *Only after she left did he speak.* (не ~~Only after did she leave~~).

## Нюансы
- После **not a single, not once** инверсия тоже есть: *Not a single word did she say.*
- Если отрицательное слово — **подлежащее**, инверсии нет: *Nobody knew.* *No one has called.*
- **Hardly, scarcely, barely** сами уже отрицательны: ~~Hardly had he not left~~. Двойного отрицания не должно быть.
- В вопросах инверсия — обычная: *Why did she leave?* Здесь же речь о *утвердительных* предложениях.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~Never I have seen such courage.~~ → Never **have I** seen such courage.
- ~~Rarely she complains.~~ → Rarely **does she** complain.
- ~~Not only he apologised.~~ → Not only **did he apologise**.
- ~~Hardly had she left than he called.~~ → Hardly had she left **when** he called.
- ~~No sooner had we sat down when the music started.~~ → ... **than** the music started.
- ~~Only after she left, did he speak.~~ → Only after she left **did he speak**. (без запятой, инверсия в главной части)
en:
## What is inversion after adverbials
The normal word order is subject first, then verb: *I have never seen it.* If we move a **negative or limiting adverbial** (never, rarely, hardly, not only...) to the front, we get **inversion**: the auxiliary verb moves in front of the subject, as in a question, but the sentence stays a statement.
> I have **never** seen such a beautiful sunset. → **Never have I** seen such a beautiful sunset.
> She **rarely** complains. → **Rarely does she** complain.
Inversion makes speech more emphatic and formal. It is common in writing, speeches and formal texts, and sounds bookish in everyday conversation.

## How inversion is built
1. The adverbial comes first.
2. Auxiliary or modal verb: *have, had, was, is, can, should, must*...
3. Subject.
4. Main verb.
If the ordinary sentence has no auxiliary (Present Simple, Past Simple), we add **do / does / did** and the main verb becomes an infinitive: *She never lies.* → *Never does she lie.* *They rarely came.* → *Rarely did they come.* With **be** we add nothing: *Rarely is he late.*

## Which adverbials trigger inversion
- **Negative and frequency adverbials**: **never, rarely, seldom, hardly ever, nowhere, at no time, in no way, on no account, under no circumstances**.
> **Under no circumstances should** you open this door.
> **Nowhere is** the problem more serious than in the south.
- **little** (meaning "not at all"): ***Little did** he know that the company was about to collapse.*
- **hardly / scarcely ... when** and **no sooner ... than** (both mean "as soon as"): ***Hardly had** she left **when** he called.* — ***No sooner had** she left **than** he called.* We use **than** after no sooner and **when** after hardly / scarcely; the first part usually has the past perfect.
- **not only ... but (also)**: ***Not only did** he apologise, **but** he also sent flowers.* Only the first part is inverted.
- **not until / only after / only when / only then / only by**: ***Not until** the 1960s **did** the idea become popular.* — ***Only then did** I realise my mistake.* — ***Only by working** hard **can** you succeed.* The inversion is in the **main** clause, not in the clause with until/after/when: *Only after she left did he speak.* (not ~~Only after did she leave~~).

## Details
- After **not a single, not once** we also use inversion: *Not a single word did she say.*
- If the negative word is the **subject**, there is no inversion: *Nobody knew.* *No one has called.*
- **Hardly, scarcely, barely** are already negative, so avoid a double negative: ~~Hardly had he not left~~.
- In questions inversion is normal: *Why did she leave?* Here we are talking about *statements*.

## Common mistakes
- ~~Never I have seen such courage.~~ → Never **have I** seen such courage.
- ~~Rarely she complains.~~ → Rarely **does she** complain.
- ~~Not only he apologised.~~ → Not only **did he apologise**.
- ~~Hardly had she left than he called.~~ → Hardly had she left **when** he called.
- ~~No sooner had we sat down when the music started.~~ → ... **than** the music started.
- ~~Only after she left, did he speak.~~ → Only after she left **did he speak**. (no comma; inversion in the main clause)
structure:
## Схема инверсии
> **наречие** + **вспомогательный глагол** + **подлежащее** + основной глагол
> Never **have** I seen it · Rarely **does** she smile · Only then **did** we understand

## Наречия и модели
| Наречие | Модель | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| never, rarely, seldom, hardly ever | adv + aux + S + V | Seldom do we see such skill. |
| little | Little + did + S + V | Little did he know... |
| no sooner ... than | No sooner + had + S + V3 ... than | No sooner had I left than it rained. |
| hardly / scarcely ... when | Hardly + had + S + V3 ... when | Hardly had I left when it rained. |
| not only ... but also | Not only + aux + S + V, but ... | Not only did she win, but she also broke the record. |
| not until / only after / only when | adv-фраза + aux + S + V | Not until May did he reply. |
| under no circumstances, on no account, at no time | adv + modal + S + V | Under no circumstances must you leave. |

## Нет вспомогательного — добавляем do
| Обычный порядок | Инверсия |
|---|---|
| She never lies. | Never does she lie. |
| They rarely came. | Rarely did they come. |
| He is seldom late. | Seldom is he late. |

exercises.title: Вставьте вспомогательный глагол
exercises.instruction: Вставьте нужное слово. В скобках — варианты, из которых нужно выбрать.

items.text: Never {{have}} I met anyone so generous.
Rarely {{does}} she complain about her workload.
No sooner had the film started {{than}} the power went out.
Hardly had we arrived {{when}} it began to pour.
Not only {{did}} he forget my birthday, but he also forgot the party.
Little {{did}} they know that the company was about to go bankrupt.
Only after the results were published {{did}} the scientists realise the error.
Under no circumstances {{are}} passengers allowed to open the doors.
Not until midnight {{did}} the guests leave.
{{Seldom|Rarely|Hardly ever}} do we see such dedication. (= not often)
Only when the lights went out {{did}} we notice the stars.
At no time {{was}} the public in any danger.
Not a single word {{did}} she say during the meeting.
Nowhere in the report {{is|was}} the problem mentioned.
No sooner {{had}} I closed the door than the phone rang.
Not only is the flat expensive, {{but}} it is also tiny.

items.q: Hardly ___ the building when the alarm went off.
Not until the 19th century ___ widely available.
Only then ___ how serious the situation was.
items.why: **Only then did she realise** — основной глагол в инфинитиве.

items.q: Seldom ___ such talent in one person.
Under no circumstances ___ the lift during a fire.
items.why: Модальный глагол выходит вперёд: **should you use**.

items.q: Not only ___ late, but she also forgot the documents.
items.why: С глаголом be: **was she**, без do.

items.q: No sooner had we sat down ___ the music started.

options: Rarely I have seen such courage.
Rarely have I seen such courage.
Rarely I saw have such courage.
Hardly had she left than he called.
Hardly had she left when he called.
Hardly she had left when he called.
Only after dinner did he tell us the news.
Only after dinner he told us the news.
Only after dinner told he us the news.
items.why: После Only after + фраза — **did he tell**.

options: Not only did he apologise, he also sent flowers.
Not only he apologised, he also sent flowers.
Not only apologised he, he also sent flowers.
Little did I know what was waiting for me.
Little I knew what was waiting for me.
Little I did know what was waiting for me.
In no way he is responsible.
In no way is he responsible.
In no way is responsible he.

exercises.title: Начните предложение с наречия
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, начав его с указанного слова.

items.prompt: Start with **Never**: I have never seen such an elegant solution.
answers: Never have I seen such an elegant solution.

items.prompt: Start with **Rarely**: She rarely takes a day off.
answers: Rarely does she take a day off.

items.prompt: Start with **No sooner**: As soon as he sat down, the phone rang.
answers: No sooner had he sat down than the phone rang.

items.prompt: Start with **Hardly**: She had hardly begun to speak when the audience started to laugh.
answers: Hardly had she begun to speak when the audience started to laugh.
Hardly had she begun to speak when the audience started laughing.

items.prompt: Start with **Not only**: He is a talented pianist and he also composes music.
answers: Not only is he a talented pianist, but he also composes music.
Not only is he a talented pianist but he also composes music.
Not only is he a talented pianist, he also composes music.
Not only is he a talented pianist, but he composes music too.
Not only is he a talented pianist but he composes music too.

items.prompt: Start with **Only after**: We checked the data, and then we noticed the mistake.
answers: Only after we checked the data did we notice the mistake.
Only after checking the data did we notice the mistake.
Only after we had checked the data did we notice the mistake.

exercises.title: Усильте высказывание
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение с инверсией, начав с указанных слов.

items.prompt: Start with **Not until**: She didn't realise the danger until the water reached the door.
answers: Not until the water reached the door did she realise the danger.
Not until the water had reached the door did she realise the danger.
Not until the water reached the door did she realize the danger.
Not until the water had reached the door did she realize the danger.

items.prompt: Start with **Little did he**: He had no idea that he was being watched. (know)
answers: Little did he know that he was being watched.
Little did he know he was being watched.

items.prompt: Start with **Under no circumstances**: You must not open this door.
answers: Under no circumstances must you open this door.
Under no circumstances should you open this door.

items.prompt: Start with **Seldom**: We seldom get such good service.
answers: Seldom do we get such good service.
Seldom do we receive such good service.

items.prompt: Start with **At no time**: The staff never mentioned the problem to the customers.
answers: At no time did the staff mention the problem to the customers.

items.prompt: Start with **Only when**: She read the contract carefully and then she saw the problem.
answers: Only when she read the contract carefully did she see the problem.
Only when she had read the contract carefully did she see the problem.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Напишите предложения с инверсией по образцу.

items.prompt: Write about something you have never done. Start with **Never have I**.
items.sample: Never have I travelled alone to another continent.

items.prompt: Write about something you rarely do. Start with **Rarely do I**.
items.sample: Rarely do I watch television in the evening.

items.prompt: Write about an event after which you understood something important. Start with **Only after** or **Only then**.
items.sample: Only after I moved abroad did I understand how much I missed my family.

items.prompt: Write about a surprise. Start with **No sooner had I ... than**.
items.sample: No sooner had I sat down than my phone started ringing.

items.prompt: Write about two good things about your city. Start with **Not only**.
items.sample: Not only is my city beautiful, but it is also very safe.
